plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 1857, 1894 & 11 Jan 1897 (Louis Pasteur claims fermentation requires living yeast; Emil Fischer proposes the Lock-and-Key enzyme model; Eduard Buchner crushes yeast at 300 atm and discovers cell-free Zymase fermentation, winning the 1907 Nobel Prize) · Aug 1926 & 20 Jul 1930 (James Sumner crystallises jack-bean urease with one arm and John Howard Northrop crystallises pepsin, proving enzymes are pure proteins and winning the 1946 Nobel Prize) · Feb 1958 & 22 May 1965 (Daniel Koshland proposes the Induced-Fit flexible active site; David Phillips & Louise Johnson solve the first 2-angstrom 3D X-ray structure of an enzyme, hen egg-white lysozyme).

teach_overlay.label: 1857–1965 ENZYMES TIMELINE · STRUCTURE-BASED DRUG DESIGN (ASPIRIN BLOCKING COX & PENICILLIN BLOCKING BACTERIAL TRANSPEPTIDASE)
teach_overlay.detail: Animated timeline (1857 → 1965) alongside an inked diagram of competitive and suicide enzyme inhibition showing aspirin and penicillin plugging target active-site keyholes
teach_overlay.scale: from a 300-atmosphere yeast press in Munich to an X-ray beam in London, scientists proved that life's chemistry needs no magic vital force — only folded protein machines that bend molecules across the finish line
